- Develop frontend features with Ant Design and TanStack Query.
- Build and consume REST APIs and work with PostgreSQL and ORM tooling.
- Maintain CI/CD workflows using GitHub Actions and Docker.
- Work with authentication/session management, Redis-based queues, and cloud storage.
Key Requirements:
- 5+ years in the React ecosystem with mandatory Next.js App Router experience.
- 5+ years of TypeScript with strict typing.
- Strong PostgreSQL, REST API, Git, and ORM experience; Prisma preferred.
- Experience with Ant Design 5 and TanStack Query v5.
- Knowledge of NextAuth, Redis/BullMQ, AWS S3, Docker, and GitHub Actions.
Tech Stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Prisma/ORM, REST APIs, Ant Design, TanStack Query, NextAuth, Redis/BullMQ, AWS S3, Docker, GitHub Actions

codingChallenges.title: 1. Email Address Validator
codingChallenges.problemStatement: Write a function validateEmail(email) that returns true when the supplied email has a valid basic email structure and false otherwise. The validator should reject empty values and obvious malformed inputs.
codingChallenges.validCodeCriteria: A valid solution should return true for normal addresses such as user@example.com and false for malformed examples. It should handle null/empty input safely.
codingChallenges.validImplementationExample: function validateEmail(email) { if (typeof email !== 'string') return false; const pattern = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/; return pattern.test(email); }

codingChallenges.title: 2. Next.js API Route Returning HTTP 200
codingChallenges.problemStatement: Create a simple Next.js App Router API endpoint at app/api/health/route.js. A GET request to /api/health must return JSON containing a status field with the value "ok" and an HTTP 200 response.
codingChallenges.validCodeCriteria: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 and JSON such as { "status": "ok" }. It should not return HTML or a client-side page.
codingChallenges.validImplementationExample: import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'; export async function GET() { return NextResponse.json({ status: 'ok' }, { status: 200 }); }

codingChallenges.title: 3. Find the First Non-Repeating Character
codingChallenges.problemStatement: Write a function firstUniqueChar(str) that returns the first character that appears exactly once in the input string. If no character is unique, return null.
codingChallenges.validCodeCriteria: The solution must count character frequencies and then preserve the original order when finding the first character with frequency 1. It should work for an empty string.
codingChallenges.validImplementationExample: function firstUniqueChar(str) { const freq = {}; for (const ch of str) freq[ch] = (freq[ch] || 0) + 1; for (const ch of str) if (freq[ch] === 1) return ch; return null; }
